Car $B$ is being driven due south toward Caltech at a speed of $60\,\text{km/h},$ while car $A$ is being driven due east away from Caltech. When car $B$ is $0.6\,\text{km}$ away from Caltech, car $A$ is $0.8\,\text{km}$ from Caltech. If the distance between the two vehicles is increasing at a rate of $20\,\text{km/h},$ what is the speed of car $A?$

activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Related Rates Using the Pythagorean Theorem

feedback.problem:
A $15\text{ ft}$ painter’s plank leans against a wall. The bottom end slides horizontally away from the wall at a constant rate of $3\text{ ft/s}.$ How fast is the top end sliding down the wall at the instant when it is $9\text{ ft}$ above the ground? Assume the rate at which the top slides downward is **positive**.

The top end is sliding down at a speed of 
{{field-1}} $\text{ft/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by drawing a diagram of the problem.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14066033/assets/afdb53c3134f18add3b07400805c76a36f3f7a6b8265a3f32e9e0dfaf1dd36e9.png)

In the diagram, 

- $x$ is the distance between the bottom of the plank and the wall,

- $y$ is the distance between the top of the plank and the ground, and

- $z$ is the length of the plank.

As shown in the diagram, $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ form a right triangle with $z$ as the hypotenuse. We wish to find the rate of change of $y,$ which is $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ 

We know that $y=9\,\text{ft}$ and $z=15\,\text{ft}.$ We can find $x$ using the Pythagorean Theorem, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2} & ={z}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}+{9}^{2} & ={15}^{2} \\ {x}^{2} & =225-81 \\ {x}^{2} & =144 \\ x & =12\,\text{ft}\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that:

- $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=3\,\text{ft}/\text{s},$

- The length of the plank remains the same, so $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}=0.$

Finally, we differentiate both sides of ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}={z}^{2}$ with respect to $t$ and then substitute in the known values:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({z}^{2}) \\ 2x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}+2y\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2z\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} \\ 2(12)(3)+2(9)\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2(15)(0) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-\frac{72}{18} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the top end of the plank is sliding down at a speed of $4\,\text{ft/s}.$
